newsitem.title: GREECE: RALLYING-MCRAE FORCED OUT OF ACROPOLIS RALLY AFTER ACCIDENT.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-MCRAE FORCED OUT OF ACROPOLIS RALLY AFTER ACCIDENT.

text.p: Finn Tommi Makinen, the reigning world champion, moved a step closer to retaining his crown on Sunday when title rival Briton Colin McRae was forced out of the Acropolis Rally.
McRae, who drives for Subaru, had set the fastest time on the first stage at Ipsilantis and was pushing hard on the second stage when he ran wide on the gravel surface and hit a bank.

The impact pushed the steering rack violently to one side and bent the steering column. Although McRae was able to continue for a short time, he was finally forced to retire when the column joint broke under the pressure.
His retirement boosted Makinen, who started the rally, the eighth round of this year's world championship, with a slender six points advantage in the title chase over McRae.
Although the Subaru team was hit by McRae's retirement, Sweden's Kenneth Eriksson gave them a small consolation by taking the overall lead of the event at the end of the fourth stage.

The winner of this year's Swedish Rally had traded times with Makinen and Spain's Carlos Sainz on the opening three stages, before setting the fastest time on the fourth stage to move to the top of the times.

Makinen, who led the rally at the end of the second and third stages, currently lies second overall, just two seconds behind Eriksson, with Finland's Juha Kankunnen impressing in the Ford to end the fourth stage third, just ahead of Sainz.
